A baby with SCID has very low TRECs on newborn screening.

Which cells are primarily affected?

options.label: A
options.explanation: B cells — incorrect in this context. The clinical scenario best fits T cells.

options.explanation: TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles) are byproducts of T cell maturation in the thymus. Low TRECs indicate absent or diminished T cell development.

context:
TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles) are tiny loops of DNA cut out of the genome each time a thymocyte successfully rearranges its T-cell receptor.

SCID is fundamentally a T-cell defect — although B-cell and NK-cell numbers vary by genetic subtype (X-linked, ADA, JAK3, etc.), the universal feature is failed T-cell development.
